chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about walnuts which one is unable to count, so they are measured with a measure, and what is in it is counted, then what remains is measured according to that count, so he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: How to sell nuts by volume when counting is difficult?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of selling walnuts by volume (kayl) when precise counting is impractical, provided the measurement for the remainder is proportionally calculated based on the initial sample. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) in commercial transactions by allowing reasonable estimation (takhmin) when exact enumeration is burdensome. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic contract law in accommodating practical realities while maintaining fairness and transparency in trade.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked

about the walnuts which I was unable to count, so it is measured with a measure, and it is counted whatever was in it, then what remained was counted upon the counting of that, from the numbering. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked
about walnuts that cannot be counted. The owner weighs a certain measurement, then counts the rest according to that measurement. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
